title: Edit-time standards load as native path-scoped rules where they can
body:
Source: code.claude.com glossary (Rules). Files in .claude/rules/ with a paths: frontmatter load natively only when Claude reads, writes or edits a matching file. KRN does the same through a PreToolUse hook that injects 'Standards for editing X' on every tool call, which costs one hook process per call (ADR 0022 targets hook p50 <= 60 ms).
Outcome: .krn/runs/lead/native-rules-verdict.md states PASS or FAIL. PASS needs native path-scoped rules rendered from .agents/standards.json for Read/Edit/Write to keep edit recall of all labels >= 0.76 and cut hook p50 per call. Bash commands that name files stay on the hook. On PASS the rendering ships.
Proof: krn doctor --hooks p50 before and after, and edit recall of all labels not below 0.76 (#1388).
Files: .claude/rules/, src/hook/, .agents/standards.json
